title: A 52-year-old female who is a patient from your practice is treated for stage I gingival squamous cell carcinoma.  Six-months after her therapy she presents to your office for a regular check-up. She has a 17-year-old daughter and she is concerned that she too may suffer from oral squamous cell carcinoma.  She heard about a vaccine called Gardasil 9 that is effective in preventing human papilloma virus (HPV) infection.  She was under the impression that her gingival squamous cell carcinoma may have been caused by HPV.  She wants to know if you think her daughter should get this vaccine to help prevent oral squamous cell carcinoma.  Which of the following represents the most accurate response to her question?
Oral Pathology Exam 1 (Spring 2018): Most cancers like yours are not caused by HPV.  However, Gardasil 9 is proven to prevent HPV-related squamous cell carcinomas in the oropharynx.
oralpath: Your cancer was most likely caused by HPV 16.  Infection by this HPV subtype in the oral cavity is prevented by Gardasil 9 and will be extremely effective in preventing an oral cancer from developing in your daughter.
exam1: Most oral squamous cell carcinomas like the one you had are not caused by HPV.  Gardasil 9 is known to be effective in preventing squamous cell carcinomas in other areas of the body.  Whether it prevents oral squamous cell carcinoma or oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma is yet to be determined.
column5: Most squamous cell carcinomas of the head and neck are caused by HPV.  Your daughter will definitely benefit from getting the Gardasil 9 vaccine.
